attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post, part of his chain of dependencies.

semantics.note: Faithful. It keeps 'dictated by' and 'ability to raise debt'. 'Is going to be' makes it a firm, forward-looking causal claim with no deadline, so treating it as a forecast with an open horizon is reasonable.

contract.note: Reading 'dictated' as a determining constraint on borrowing access is a fair, ordinary reading. Requiring lender evidence that separates AI sentiment from collateral and credit conditions is demanding, but it matches the strength of the claim.

evidence.note: SoftBank's 2026 annual report CFO message (dated 2026-07-27, before the cutoff). It credits financing access to LTV discipline and lender relationships, and notes that credit depends on NAV. This is management's own view, not a causal finding, so it is context only.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and no dated financing episode with lender evidence shows AI sentiment either deciding or not deciding SoftBank's access to debt. The CFO's account is a company disclosure and cannot settle the causal question. The early-resolution rule is not met, so the claim stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence about CoreWeave in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithful. The normalisation keeps the present-tense liquidity shortfall and both links in the chain: loans depend on contracts, and contracts depend on expansion.

contract.note: Counting cash plus drawable facilities as liquidity is a fair reading. Year-end 2024 is a reasonable proxy for 'currently' in March 2025, and the contract admits the gap. Requiring both dependencies to be documented is fair.

evidence.note: CoreWeave's FY2025 10-K gives year-end 2024 liquidity of about $5.8B (cash plus facility availability). There is no matching schedule of required expansion spending, so a shortfall can be neither shown nor ruled out.
OpenAI contract announcement dated 2025-03-10, worth up to $11.9B. Contract value is not spending need or liquidity, and it says nothing about loan conditions.

reviews.rationale: Year-end 2024 liquidity is known, but no admitted evidence sets out the spending the expansion required, and no lending or customer agreement was verified for the claimed dependencies. The evidence neither shows a shortfall nor shows enough funding.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post. The figure is his estimate.

semantics.note: A causal claim (paying CoreWeave depends on raising money) resting on a dated numerical premise (losses over $14B in 2025). Both parts are kept.

contract.note: Reading the dependency as necessary is fair. Which loss measure is used decides the numerical part: headline net, operating, and adjusted losses fall on different sides of $14B. The contract rightly flags this and the cash-burn alternative.

evidence.note: Ars Technica (June 2026) reports audited 2025 figures: operating loss about $20.9B, and headline net loss near $39B including a one-off charge, or about $8B without it. The result depends on the basis chosen, and none of it shows whether CoreWeave payments needed new funding.

reviews.rationale: The loss figure exceeds $14B on headline net and operating measures but falls below it once the one-off charge is excluded, and the speaker named no basis. More importantly, no reconciliation of cash against obligations shows whether OpenAI could pay CoreWeave without new fundraising, so the core causal claim is not settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithful: a universal present-tense claim that nobody but NVIDIA profits from generative AI, with the NVIDIA exemption kept.

contract.note: Reading profit as earnings after costs, across the whole generative AI business, is fair. Calendar 2024 is a reasonable proxy for 'is making'. The contract says the post exempts Turing elsewhere; the excerpt shown cannot confirm that, but the outcome is the same either way.

evidence.note: A LinkedIn post by Turing's CEO (about Feb 2025) says Turing became profitable in 2024. This is a company statement about itself with no stated measure, and Turing may be exempted in the post, so it is a lead rather than a finding.
Turing press release (2025-01-28) describing AI-related business lines and saying it hit profitability. It gives no profit figure, no basis, and no generative-AI share.

reviews.rationale: The only possible counterexample, Turing, rests on the company's own statement with no measure or amount, and the contract says the post exempts Turing. No independent evidence shows any non-exempt company earning a defined profit from generative AI in 2024, and none confirms the universal claim either.
